title: Drinking water secondary standards and lead free plumbing practice questions
description: Free practice questions on 40 CFR Part 143: secondary drinking water standards and lead free pipes, fittings, solder and flux, each linked to the rule.

questions.topic: Purpose and status of secondary standards
questions.question: How does 143.1 describe the federal status of the National Secondary Drinking Water Regulations?

options.A: They are Federally enforceable maximum contaminant levels for every public water system
options.B: They are not Federally enforceable but are intended as guidelines for the States
options.C: They are Federally enforceable only for community water systems
options.D: They become Federally enforceable once a system exceeds a level twice in a year

questions.explanation: 143.1 states: "The regulations in this subpart are not Federally enforceable but are intended as guidelines for the States."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.1, Purpose (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The regulations in this subpart are not Federally enforceable but are intended as guidelines for the States.

questions.topic: Purpose and status of secondary standards
questions.question: According to 143.1, the contaminants controlled by the secondary regulations primarily affect what?

options.A: The aesthetic qualities relating to the public acceptance of drinking water
options.B: The acute microbial safety of drinking water
options.C: The structural life of treatment plant equipment
options.D: The radiological quality of source water

questions.explanation: 143.1 says these regulations "control contaminants in drinking water that primarily affect the aesthetic qualities relating to the public acceptance of drinking water."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.1, Purpose (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: control contaminants in drinking water that primarily affect the aesthetic qualities relating to the public acceptance of drinking water

questions.topic: Purpose and status of secondary standards
questions.question: Under the 143.2(f) definition, the SMCL is the maximum permissible level of a contaminant in water delivered where?

options.A: At the raw water intake of the source
options.B: At the entry point to the distribution system
options.C: To the free flowing outlet of the ultimate user of public water system
options.D: At the treatment plant's finished water reservoir

questions.explanation: 143.2(f): the SMCL means "the maximum permissible level of a contaminant in water which is delivered to the free flowing outlet of the ultimate user of public water system."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.2, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The SMCL means the maximum permissible level of a contaminant in water which is delivered to the free flowing outlet of the ultimate user of public water system.

questions.topic: Purpose and status of secondary standards
questions.question: 143.2(f) excludes contaminants added to the water under circumstances controlled by the user. Which contaminants does it keep in the definition anyway?

options.A: Those added by a home water softener
options.B: Those added by a point-of-use filter the user installed
options.C: Those added by a chemical feeder the user installed at the tap
options.D: Those resulting from corrosion of piping and plumbing caused by water quality

questions.explanation: Contaminants added under circumstances controlled by the user are excluded, "except those resulting from corrosion of piping and plumbing caused by water quality."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.2, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Contaminants added to the water under circumstances controlled by the user, except those resulting from corrosion of piping and plumbing caused by water quality, are excluded from this definition.

questions.question: What does 143.3 say States may do with the secondary levels listed in its table?

options.A: Establish higher or lower levels appropriate to local conditions, provided public health and welfare are not adversely affected
options.B: Only adopt the listed levels exactly as written
options.C: Only establish lower levels, never higher ones
options.D: Establish higher levels only for systems serving fewer than 25 people

questions.explanation: The levels "represent reasonable goals for drinking water quality. The States may establish higher or lower levels" dependent upon local conditions, "provided that public health and welfare are not adversely affected."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.3, Secondary maximum contaminant levels (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The States may establish higher or lower levels which may be appropriate dependent upon local conditions such as unavailability of alternate source waters or other compelling factors, provided that public health and welfare are not adversely affected.

questions.question: In which unit does the 143.3 table express the secondary level for color?
questions.explanation: The 143.3 table lists color at "15 color units."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.3, Secondary maximum contaminant levels (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Color 15 color units.

questions.question: Which entry in the 143.3 table has the level "Non-corrosive" instead of a number?
questions.explanation: The 143.3 table lists "Corrosivity Non-corrosive." pH has a numeric range, and copper and TDS are in mg/l.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.3, Secondary maximum contaminant levels (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Corrosivity Non-corrosive.

questions.question: What pH range does the 143.3 table list as the secondary level?
questions.explanation: The 143.3 table lists "pH 6.5-8.5."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.3, Secondary maximum contaminant levels (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 143.19(c)(2), which manufacturers or importers may elect to self-certify a custom fabricated product?

options.A: Any manufacturer or importer, regardless of the number of persons employed by the manufacturer
options.B: Only manufacturers having fewer than 10 employees
options.C: Only manufacturers already certified by an ANSI accredited body

questions.explanation: 143.19(c)(2): manufacturers or importers "may elect to self-certify any custom fabricated product" in lieu of third party certification, "regardless of the number of persons employed by the manufacturer."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.19, Required certification of products (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: (2) Manufacturers or importers may elect to self-certify any custom fabricated product in lieu of obtaining certification from an ANSI accredited third party certification body, regardless of the number of persons employed by the manufacturer.

questions.question: What period does 143.19(a) set for manufacturers or importers to maintain documentation substantiating a product's certification?

options.A: 1 year after the product is discontinued
options.B: 3 years from the date of certification
options.C: At least 5 years from the date of the last sale of the product by the manufacturer or importer
options.D: 2 years from the date of first sale

questions.explanation: They "must maintain documentation to substantiate the certification for at least 5 years from the date of the last sale of the product by the manufacturer or importer."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.19, Required certification of products (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Such manufacturers or importers must maintain documentation to substantiate the certification for at least 5 years from the date of the last sale of the product by the manufacturer or importer.

questions.question: Which product does 143.19(a)(3) say does not need to be certified?
questions.explanation: 143.19(a)(3) states: "Dishwashers do not need to be certified."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.19, Required certification of products (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: (3) Dishwashers do not need to be certified.

questions.question: Under 143.4(b), measurement of pH, copper and fluoride to determine compliance under 143.3 may be conducted with one of the methods in which section?
questions.explanation: 143.4(b): "Measurement of pH, copper and fluoride to determine compliance under § 143.3 may be conducted with one of the methods in § 141.23(k)(1)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.4, Monitoring (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Measurement of pH, copper and fluoride to determine compliance under § 143.3 may be conducted with one of the methods in § 141.23(k)(1).

questions.question: Besides people who introduce products into commerce, to whom does 143.10(a) say Subpart B also applies?

options.B: Any person who uses these products in the installation or repair of a public water system or a residential or nonresidential facility providing water for human consumption
options.C: Only licensed plumbers working on community water systems
options.D: Only owners of buildings built after September 1, 2020

questions.explanation: 143.10(a): "It also applies to any person who uses these products in the installation or repair of" a public water system or "A residential or nonresidential facility providing water for human consumption."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.10, Applicability and scope (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: It also applies to any person who uses these products in the installation or repair of: (1) A public water system; or (2) A residential or nonresidential facility providing water for human consumption.

questions.question: What weighted average lead limit does 143.12(a)(2) set for "lead free" with respect to the wetted surfaces of pipes, pipe fittings, plumbing fittings and fixtures?
questions.explanation: Lead free means "Not more than a weighted average of 0.25 percent lead when used with respect to the wetted surfaces of pipes, pipe fittings, plumbing fittings, and fixtures."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.12, Definition of lead free and calculation methodology (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: (2) Not more than a weighted average of 0.25 percent lead when used with respect to the wetted surfaces of pipes, pipe fittings, plumbing fittings, and fixtures.

questions.question: When the lead content of a material is provided as a range, which value does 143.12(b) say must be used in the weighted average calculation?

options.A: The maximum content of the range
options.B: The minimum content of the range
options.D: The average of the manufacturer's test results

questions.explanation: 143.12(b): "For lead content of materials that are provided as a range, the maximum content of the range must be used."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.12, Definition of lead free and calculation methodology (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: For lead content of materials that are provided as a range, the maximum content of the range must be used.

questions.question: A fixture contains a filter with activated carbon. How does 143.12(e) treat the filter media when calculating the product's weighted average lead content?

options.A: The media count double toward the total wetted surface area
options.B: The media must be tested separately against the 0.2 percent limit
options.C: The media are not to be used in determining the total wetted surface area of the entire product
options.D: The media replace the housing in the calculation

questions.explanation: 143.12(e): media contained in filters "are not to be used in determining the “total wetted surface area of the entire product”" in paragraph (b).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.12, Definition of lead free and calculation methodology (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: (e) If a fixture contains any media (e.g., activated carbon, ion exchange resin) contained in filters, the media are not to be used in determining the “total wetted surface area of the entire product” in paragraph (b) of this section.

questions.question: What does 143.13(b) exclude from the use prohibition in 143.13(a)?

options.A: Solder used for emergency repairs of copper service lines
options.C: Water meters owned by the public water system
options.D: Leaded joints necessary for the repair of cast iron pipes

questions.explanation: 143.13(b): "Paragraph (a) of this section shall not apply to leaded joints necessary for the repair of cast iron pipes."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.13, Use prohibitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: (b) Paragraph (a) of this section shall not apply to leaded joints necessary for the repair of cast iron pipes.

questions.question: Under 143.14, enforcing the use prohibitions is a condition of what for States?

options.A: Receiving a full allotment of Public Water System Supervision grants under section 1443(a)
options.B: Keeping primary enforcement responsibility for the Revised Total Coliform Rule
options.C: Receiving Drinking Water State Revolving Fund loans for lead service line replacement
options.D: Approval of the State's operator certification program

questions.explanation: "As a condition of receiving a full allotment of Public Water System Supervision grants under section 1443(a) of the Safe Drinking Water Act, States must enforce" the requirements, through State or local plumbing codes or other means.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.14, State enforcement of use prohibitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: As a condition of receiving a full allotment of Public Water System Supervision grants under section 1443(a) of the Safe Drinking Water Act, States must enforce the requirements of section 1417(a)(1)

questions.question: Under 143.15(b), which persons engaged in the business of selling plumbing supplies are excepted from the ban on selling solder or flux that is not lead free?
questions.explanation: 143.15(b): "No person engaged in the business of selling plumbing supplies in the United States, except manufacturers, may sell solder or flux that is not lead free." Such solder or flux must still carry the 143.18 label.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.15, Introduction into commerce prohibitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: (b) No person engaged in the business of selling plumbing supplies in the United States, except manufacturers, may sell solder or flux that is not lead free

questions.question: What size condition does 143.16(b) set for water distribution main gate valves to be exempt?
questions.explanation: 143.16(b) exempts "water distribution main gate valves (provided that such valves are 2 inches in diameter or larger)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 143.16, Exemptions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: water distribution main gate valves (provided that such valves are 2 inches in diameter or larger)
